sDescription: Steve Cropper, an American guitarist, songwriter, and record producer, passed away in Nashville at age 84. As the guitarist for the Stax Records house band Booker T. & the M.G.'s, he provided accompaniment for Otis Redding, Wilson Pickett, Sam & Dave, Carla Thomas, Rufus Thomas, and Johnnie Taylor, while also producing records for many of them. Cropper subsequently joined the Blues Brothers band and collaborated with numerous musicians, such as Rod Stewart, Ringo Starr, Paul Simon, Leon Russell, Dolly Parton, John Lennon, and Harry Nilsson.

American drummer Melvin Parker died. He and his brother, saxophonist Maceo Parker, were key members of James Brown's band. Parker was the drummer on three of Brown's recordings: ‘Out of Sight,’ ‘Papa's Got A Brand New Bag,’ and ‘I Got You (I Feel Good).’

Gladstone Anderson, a Jamaican pianist, keyboard player, and singer also known as "Gladdy," passed away at the age of 81. He contributed significantly to Jamaica's musical history by helping shape the ska sound and the rocksteady beat. Aside from performing on hundreds of recordings, he led Gladdy's All Stars, the group behind the instrumental hit "The Liquidator," which charted in 1969 and 1980.

American singer-songwriter and musician Scott Weiland passed away at the age of 48. He experienced a cardiac arrest on his tour bus located in Bloomington, Minnesota, prior to an intended performance with his group The Wildabouts. Weiland gained his greatest recognition fronting Stone Temple Pilots between 1986 and 2013 and Velvet Revolver from 2003 to 2008.

English keyboard instrumentalist Ian McLagan passed away from a stroke at the age of 69. He played in Small Faces and the Faces, and collaborated with various other musicians such as The Rolling Stones, Bob Dylan, Bonnie Raitt, Joe Cocker, Billy Bragg, Jackson Browne, Chuck Berry, and Bruce Springsteen.

Ed Sheeran, a 23-year-old singer-songwriter, was designated the top global streamed artist on Spotify after accumulating over 860 million streams, surpassing Eminem in second place and Coldplay in third. Meanwhile, Katy Perry claimed the title of the year's most-streamed female artist, followed by Ariana Grande in second and Lana Del Rey in third.

Rolling Stone Ronnie Wood received a police caution in Esher, Surrey, following his arrest on suspicion of assault. A passer-by had called 999 during a violent dispute between Wood and Ekaterina Ivanova, his 21-year-old on-off girlfriend.

Derek Wadsworth, who worked as a composer, keyboardist, and arranger, passed away in Oxfordshire, England. Throughout his career as a musician, he collaborated with Georgie Fame, Alan Price, George Harrison, Mike Oldfield, Diana Ross, Tom Jones, Dionne Warwick, and Simply Red. He also served as an arranger for David Essex, Dusty Springfield, Nina Simone, Judy Garland, Kate Bush, Cat Stevens, Rod Stewart, Small Faces, The Rolling Stones, and Manfred Mann.

Diana Ross and the Beach Boys' Brian Wilson both received recognition at the Kennedy Center Honors, an event attended by President Bush. To honor Brian Wilson, Hootie and the Blowfish performed a medley featuring several well-known Beach Boys tracks.

For the first time in their career, the reunited Take That claimed the top spot on the UK singles and album charts at the same time. While their new album Beautiful World debuted at No.1, the single 'Patience' held the number one position for a second consecutive week.

A Los Angeles court determined that singer Barbra Streisand's privacy was not breached by the publication of an image of her Malibu estate on a website. Streisand had brought a $10m lawsuit against software entrepreneur Kenneth Adelman following his posting of her home's photograph on his conservation website.

American session guitarist Grady Martin passed away at the age of 72. As part of the renowned Nashville A-Team, his guitar work featured on major hits including Marty Robbins' 'El Paso', Loretta Lynn's 'Coal Miner's Daughter', and Roy Orbison's 'Oh, Pretty Woman'. Spanning a 50-year career, Martin performed as a backing musician for artists such as Woody Guthrie, Arlo Guthrie, Joan Baez, J. J. Cale, Elvis Presley, Buddy Holly, Johnny Cash, and Patsy Cline.

American composer Hoyt Curtin passed away from heart failure at the age of 78. He wrote theme songs for numerous Hanna-Barbera cartoons, such as The Flintstones, Top Cat, Jonny Quest, Superfriends, The Jetsons, Josie and the Pussycats, and The New Scooby-Doo Movies.
Rapper Jay-Z was reported arrested concerning the stabbing of music executive Lance Rivera. He faced a charge of first-degree assault.

U2 vocalist Bono recovered his lost laptop computer after it went missing. A young man purchased the device for £300 and realized it was the missing computer, which held tracks from the upcoming U2 album.

Boyz II Men succeeded themselves at the top of the US singles chart as 'On Bended Knee' commenced a six-week tenure at No. 1. Previously, the group held the top position for a record-setting 14 weeks with 'I'll Make Love To You'.

Two families filed a lawsuit against Judas Priest, claiming the band was to blame for their sons forming a suicide pact and shooting themselves subsequent to listening to Judas Priest records. The legal representatives and parents alleged that the Judas Priest track Better By You, Better Than Me from the Stained Class album contained a subliminal message of 'do it', which they claimed incited the suicide attempt. The court proceedings ran from 16 July until 24 August 1990, resulting in the dismissal of the lawsuit.

A The Who concert at The Riverfront Coliseum in Cincinnati ended in tragedy when a stampede for unreserved seats resulted in 11 audience members being trampled to death, while another 26 fans sustained injuries. The event utilized 'festival seating,' meaning tickets offered first-come, first-served access. Outside the venue, waiting fans mistook the band's late sound check for the start of the show and rushed the doors while they were still closed.

Wings began a nine-week reign at No. 1 on the UK charts with 'Mull Of Kintyre'. This track became the initial single to surpass 2 million copies sold in the UK and was co-written by Denny Laine, who parted with his rights to the song during a period of bankruptcy.

Seven gunmen entered Bob Marley's Kingston residence and carried out an assassination attempt that resulted in injuries to Marley, his wife Rita, and manager Don Taylor, with the incident suspected to have political motives.

Algie, a 40-foot inflatable pig, drifted into the sky above London, England, after coming loose from its moorings during a photo shoot for the upcoming Pink Floyd album Animals. A warning for pilots was issued regarding the loose flying pig by the Civil Aviation Authority. The pig ultimately landed in a barn located in Godmersham, Kent, prompting a local farmer to complain that his cows had been frightened by the event.
Approximately three and a half million individuals requested tickets for upcoming British Albert Hall performances by ABBA, whereas a little more than 11 thousand tickets were actually available.

Ronnie Wood's wife Krisse and her friend Audrey Burgon were arrested following a raid at the couple's Richmond residence for alleged possession of cocaine and cannabis, with newspapers stating that both women were discovered "sleeping together."

Over the course of three days of recording sessions at Muscle Shoals studios, the Rolling Stones recorded 'Brown Sugar'. Mick Jagger wrote the track with Marsha Hunt in mind, who was his secret girlfriend and the mother of his first child, Karis. Legal disputes with the group's previous record label delayed the release of the song for over a year. The single reached No.1 in the United States and Canada, and secured the No.2 position on the charts in the United Kingdom and Ireland.

The Monkees gave their first live performance at the International Arena in Honolulu. Intense pressure to launch a touring iteration of the band had arisen from the massive success of their television show and its accompanying records.

Ray Charles received a $10,000 fine and a five-year suspended prison sentence following a conviction for heroin and marijuana possession. During his teenage years, Charles started a heroin addiction that lasted for decades.
British group The New Vaudeville Band began a three-week duration at the top of the US singles chart featuring 'Winchester Cathedral', which achieved a No.4 position in the UK.

The Beatles set out on what would be their last ever UK tour at Glasgow's Odeon Cinema. Also on the bill, The Moody Blues The Koobas and Beryl Marsden. The last show was at Cardiff's Capitol Cinema on 12th December.
During a performance at the Memorial Hall in Sacramento, California, Rolling Stone Keith Richards suffered an electric shock and lost consciousness after his guitar touched his microphone.

The Beatles sixth studio album Rubber Soul was released. Often referred to as a folk rock album, Rubber Soul incorporates a mix of pop, soul and folk musical styles. The title derives from the colloquialism "plastic soul", which referred to soul played by English musicians. Most of the songs on the album were composed soon after the Beatles' return to London following their August 1965 North American tour. The album reflects the influence of their month in America, where they set a new attendance record when they played to over 55,000 at Shea Stadium on 15 August, met Bob Dylan in New York and their longtime hero Elvis Presley in Los Angeles.

The debut studio album by The Who was issued in the UK as My Generation. Decca Records subsequently distributed the record in the United States in April 1966 under the title The Who Sings My Generation, featuring a distinct cover and a somewhat modified track list. Mojo magazine ranked the album as the second greatest guitar album of all time in 2003.

Their cover of 'Little Red Rooster' gave the Rolling Stones their second No.1 single in the UK. The band recorded the track in Chicago at Chess Studios, the location where Muddy Waters, Howlin' Wolf, and Little Walter had previously cut their blues hits.

Brian Epstein summoned The Beatles to his office to talk about potentially managing them. A 4pm gathering was attended by John Lennon, George Harrison, and Pete Best who showed up late after having drinks at the Grapes pub on Matthew Street. Meanwhile, Paul McCartney missed the appointment because Harrison stated he had only just woken up and was bathing.

Guy Mitchell secured the No. 1 position on the US singles chart with his rendition of 'Singing The Blues', maintaining the top spot for a duration of nine weeks. Nearly concurrently with Mitchell's recording, two alternative charting versions of the track appeared: one performed by the UK vocalist Tommy Steele, accompanied by the Steelmen, and another by the US country artist Marty Robbins.

Elvis Presley's debut release through RCA Victor Records was publicized, featuring the tracks 'Mystery Train' and 'I Forgot to Remember to Forget' which were acquired from Sam Phillips at Sun Records. His new label characterized him as 'The most talked about personality in recorded music in the last 10 years.'

New Zealand-British singer and songwriter Daniel Bedingfield released his debut studio album, Gotta Get thru This, in 2002. The album generated three UK No. 1 singles: "Gotta Get thru This", "If You're Not the One", and "Never Gonna Leave Your Side".
Montell Jordan is an American R&B singer, songwriter, and producer known for his 1995 single 'This Is How We Do It', which reached No.1 in the US and No.11 in the UK.
Duane Roland was a guitarist for the American Southern rock and hard rock band Molly Hatchet, known for the 1980 album 'Beatin' The Odds' and their hit song 'Flirtin' with Disaster'.
Don Barnes is an American rock vocalist and guitarist and one of the founding members of the Southern rock band 38 Special.

Mike Stock is an English songwriter, record producer, and musician. Through his work with the songwriting and production trio Stock Aitken Waterman, he has helped create more than a hundred top-40 hits in the UK, featuring 16 No.1s, and holds recognition from the Guinness World Records as one of the most successful songwriters in history. The trio received three Ivor Novello Awards in 1990 for Songwriter of the Year, Most Performed Work for 'This Time I Know It's for Real' by Donna Summer, and Best Selling A-Side for 'Too Many Broken Hearts' by Jason Donovan.

Nicky Stevens is an English singer who performs with the pop group Brotherhood of Man. In 1976, the group released the hit 'Save Your Kisses for Me', which served as the United Kingdom's entry in the Eurovision Song Contest 1976. The track achieved worldwide success by climbing to No. 1 across numerous nations, such as the UK, where it finished the year as the highest-selling single.

Kimberley Rew is a member of the British-American rock band Katrina And The Waves, which achieved widespread recognition for the 1985 hit single 'Walking on Sunshine'. Additionally, the band secured victory at the 1997 Eurovision Song Contest with their song 'Love Shine a Light'.

American rock singer Mickey Thomas is widely recognized as a lead vocalist for Jefferson Starship and Starship, groups associated with the 1987 UK and US No. 1 hit single 'Nothing's Gonna Stop Us'. Before his time with Jefferson Starship, he performed as a backing and occasional lead singer in Elvin Bishop's band. Additionally, he served as the lead vocalist on Bishop's most famous track, 'Fooled Around And Fell In Love'.

John Wilson is a drummer who played in the Irish rock and blues band Taste. Taste released the 1970 UK No.18 album 'On The Boards', and the group was founded by the musician and songwriter Rory Gallagher.

Ozzy Osbourne (John Michael Osbourne), singer and songwriter with English rock band Black Sabbath who had the 1970 UK No.4 single 'Paranoid'. The band's self-titled 1970 album was voted as the best British rock album ever by Kerrang! in 2005. He performed on the band's first eight studio albums before he was fired in 1979 due to his problems with drugs and alcohol. He had the 1986 solo UK No.20 single 'Shot In The Dark' and became the star of The Osbournes MTV show, which first aired in 2002. Osbourne sold over 100 million albums, including his solo work and Black Sabbath releases. Osbourne courted controversy throughout his career. He adopted the title "Prince of Darkness", took on a demonic stage persona, and portrayed himself as the "Madman of Rock". He died on 22 July 2025 at the age of 76, just seventeen days after his final live performance with Black Sabbath at the Back to the Beginning farewell concert.

British rock band Geordie featured guitarist Vic Malcolm and singer Brian Johnson during the group's initial 1970s activity, which included notable tracks like 'Don't Do That', 'All Because of You', 'Can You Do It', 'Electric Lady', and 'Goodbye Love'. Following the February 1980 death of AC/DC frontman Bon Scott, AC/DC selected Brian Johnson to assume lead vocal responsibilities.

English singer-songwriter and guitar player Ralph McTell is best known for his 1975 UK No.2 single 'Streets of London', which has been covered by over two hundred artists worldwide. During the 1980s, he composed and performed music for two children's television programmes, starting with Alphabet Zoo and subsequently Tickle on the Tum.

Ken Lewis was a member of the English vocal trio Ivy League, who achieved their highest recognition for the 1965 UK No.3 single 'Tossing and Turning'. Earlier, in November 1964, the group provided background vocals on the hit single 'I Can't Explain' by The Who.

Andy Williams was an American singer and television host who achieved the 1957 US and UK No.1 single 'Butterfly', the 1963 US and UK No.2 single 'Can't Get Used To Losing You', and more than 25 additional US Top 40 singles. He hosted the long-running Andy Williams TV show between 1962 and 1971 and accumulated worldwide sales of over 100 million records. At the age of 84, he passed away from bladder cancer on September 25th, 2012.
